0.0.n: A nickname for the store chain Don Quijote; it is a name.

0.2.n: Polite form of 入る; the speaker is understood to be the person entering.

1.0.n: Used alone to name the object before describing what it does.

1.2.n: Here it is the thing that opens, marked by が.

1.3.n: Marks ドア as the thing that opens.

1.4.n: Polite form of 開く, describing the door opening rather than someone opening it.

2.0.n: Used alone to name the object before describing the action.

2.2.n: Here it is the item being taken, marked by を.

2.3.n: Marks カゴ as the thing the speaker takes.

2.4.n: Polite form of 取る, used here for picking up a shopping basket.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when it is clear who is acting.

1.tip: 開きます describes the door opening, not a person opening the door.

2.tip: を marks the basket as the object of the action 取ります.
